matches.rationale: No finding mentions the inflated FT-HID dataset size (38,364 vs. the actual 9,120). The issue of dataset-size manipulation in Table 1 is not detected by any prediction.

Prediction 2 identifies the Rodrigues formula error in Equation 3, explicitly noting that the (1+cosθ) coefficient is incorrect and should be (1−cosθ), which is the exact corruption described in the ground truth.
No finding identifies the omission of training hyperparameters (batch size, learning rate schedule, warmup, weight decay, gradient clipping). This experimental reproducibility gap is not caught.
No finding challenges the 'first egocentric realistic world simulator' claim or cites prior works (Wonderland, Gen3C) that would contradict this novelty assertion in the abstract.
No finding detects the fabricated Matrix-Game [49] reference. While other citation issues are flagged (swaps, wrong attributions), this specific non-existent paper is not identified.

Prediction 16 highlights that Table 2's full-model row is labelled 'indoor scenes only' yet the identical numbers are reused as general full-benchmark results in other tables, precisely matching the ground truth's concern about selective indoor-only reporting misrepresented as full-benchmark performance.

Prediction 3 flags the undefined coefficient βt in the noising equation zt = αt z0 + βt δt ε in Equation 1, which matches the ground truth's corruption of introducing an unexplained 'β' into the diffusion formulation.

Prediction 12 identifies the unequal conditioning protocol where competitors receive LLM-enriched text captions while PlayerOne uses motion sequences, confounding the motion-alignment comparisons; this matches the ground truth's flawed experimental design concern exactly.

No finding specifically calls out that the claim of 'diverse scenarios' and large-margin superiority in Section 4.3 is based on only 100 videos from a single dataset (Nymeria) with limited outdoor or challenging conditions.
No finding addresses the deleted ethical-disclosure sentence about user anonymization and front-camera recording from the Figure 1 caption, nor flags the absence of IRB or consent information.

Prediction 11 identifies the Introduction's hyperbolic language ('completely solves ... eliminates all limitations'), which matches the ground truth's corruption replacing measured academic language with promotional, absolute claims.

Prediction 1 detects the cross-section inconsistency between the abstract's claim of 'real-time generation at 30 FPS' and the implementation details reporting only 8 FPS/~8.4 FPS, which is the same underlying issue described in the ground truth.
No finding identifies the fabricated MPJPE value of 98.42 in Table 2, which contradicts the correct 127.16 reported in Table 3. The specific numerical manipulation goes undetected.
No finding catches the dimensional inconsistency where zmotion is changed from R^{k×3×h×w} to R^{k×5×h×w}, creating a channel-count mismatch with the DiT input specification.

Prediction 11 notes the Conclusion's claim of 'coherent world generation across all scenarios without exception,' which the ground truth identifies as a contradiction with the Limitations section's documentation of degraded performance in game scenarios, making this a match.
